name: Chapter 8: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques
description: Hybridisation, structural formulas, classification, IUPAC naming, isomerism, reaction intermediates, electronic effects, purification and analysis

cards.term: What property of carbon makes organic chemistry possible?
cards.definition: Catenation: forming covalent bonds with other carbon atoms
Berzelius (Swedish chemist): organic compounds need a vital force of living things

cards.term: Correction: NCERT spells the vital-force chemist "Berzilius". Correct spelling?
cards.definition: Jöns Jacob Berzelius

cards.term: Who disproved vital force, and how?
cards.definition: F. Wöhler (1828): made urea from inorganic ammonium cyanate: NH₄CNO → NH₂CONH₂

cards.term: Who synthesised acetic acid and methane from inorganic sources?
cards.definition: Acetic acid: Kolbe (1845). Methane: Berthelot (1856).
sp³ (25% s): Tetrahedral: methane CH₄; sp² (33% s): Trigonal planar: ethene C₂H₄; sp (50% s): Linear: ethyne C₂H₂

advancedHtml.frontHtml:
Hybridisation of carbon

Shape and example?

sp³ (25% s)?
sp² (33% s)?
sp (50% s)?
advancedHtml.backHtml:
Hybridisation of carbon

Shape and example?

sp³ (25% s)Tetrahedral: methane CH₄
sp² (33% s)Trigonal planar: ethene C₂H₄
sp (50% s)Linear: ethyne C₂H₂

cards.term: How does s character affect bond length, strength and electronegativity?
cards.definition: More s character → orbital closer to nucleus: shorter, stronger bonds; higher electronegativity (sp > sp² > sp³)

cards.term: Why is rotation about C=C restricted?
cards.definition: Rotation would destroy the sideways overlap of parallel p orbitals (π bond)

cards.term: Where is the π electron cloud, and why is it reactive?
cards.definition: Above and below the molecular plane: easily available to attacking reagents

cards.term: In H₂C=CH₂, are all atoms coplanar?
cards.definition: Yes: p orbitals must be parallel, perpendicular to the molecular plane

cards.term: σ and π bonds in HC≡CCH=CHCH₃ and CH₂=C=CHCH₃? (Problem 8.1)
cards.definition: (a) 10 σ, 3 π. (b) 9 σ, 2 π.

cards.term: Hybridisation of each C in CH₃CH=CH₂? in CH₂=C=O? (Problem 8.2 style)
cards.definition: CH₃: sp³; =CH–, =CH₂: sp². Cumulated C in CH₂=C=O: sp

cards.term: Hybridisation and shape: H₂C=O, CH₃F, HC≡N? (Problem 8.3)
cards.definition: sp² trigonal planar; sp³ tetrahedral; sp linear
Complete: every bond shown as a dash. Condensed: dashes omitted, identical groups by subscripts, e.g. CH₃(CH₂)₆CH₃.
C and H not shown zig-zag lines each junction and terminal is a carbon (terminal = CH₃ unless a group is shown) heteroatoms written

cards.term: Condensed formula of HOCH₂CH₂CH₂CH(CH₃)CH(CH₃)CH₃ style chains?
cards.definition: Group repeated units: e.g. HO(CH₂)₃CH(CH₃)CH(CH₃)₂
Solid wedge: bond towards the viewer. Dashed wedge: bond away. Plain line: in the plane.
Framework (bonds only), ball-and-stick (atoms and bonds), space-filling (relative size from van der Waals radii)

cards.term: Model used for C=C compounds like ethene?
cards.definition: Ball-and-spring model
Open chain: ethane, isobutane, acetaldehyde, acetic acid
Carbon atoms in a ring with aliphatic properties: cyclopropane, cyclohexane, cyclohexene
Homocyclic: ring of carbon only. Heterocyclic: ring has other atoms, e.g. tetrahydrofuran.
Benzene, aniline, naphthalene
Tropone
Furan, thiophene, pyridine
An atom or group of atoms joined to the carbon chain that decides the characteristic chemical properties (–OH, –CHO, –COOH)
Compounds with the same functional group, a general formula, successive members differing by –CH₂–

cards.term: Origin of the common names citric acid and formic acid?
cards.definition: Citric: from citrus fruits. Formic: Latin formica = ant (red ant).
Its shape resembles the geodesic domes of architect R. Buckminster Fuller
Neopentane, formaldehyde, acetone, chloroform

cards.term: Common names of C₆H₅OCH₃, C₆H₅NH₂, C₆H₅COCH₃, CH₃OCH₂CH₃?
cards.definition: Anisole, aniline, acetophenone, ethyl methyl ether

cards.term: Old name for alkanes and its meaning?
cards.definition: Paraffins: Latin "little affinity"

cards.term: Names of C₁ to C₁₀, C₂₀ and C₃₀ straight-chain alkanes?
cards.definition: Methane … decane; icosane (C₂₀); triacontane (C₃₀)

cards.term: How is an alkyl group named?
cards.definition: Remove one H from an alkane; replace "-ane" by "-yl" (CH₄ → –CH₃ methyl)

cards.term: Structures of isopropyl, sec-butyl, isobutyl, tert-butyl, neopentyl?
cards.definition: (CH₃)₂CH– CH₃CH₂CH(CH₃)– (CH₃)₂CHCH₂– (CH₃)₃C– (CH₃)₃CCH₂–

cards.term: Two substituents in equivalent positions: which gets the lower number?
cards.definition: The one coming first alphabetically (3-ethyl-6-methyloctane, not 6-ethyl-3-methyl)

cards.term: Which prefixes count in alphabetising: iso, neo, sec, tert?
cards.definition: iso and neo count (part of the name); sec and tert do not

cards.term: Two chains of equal length: which is parent?
cards.definition: The one with more side chains

cards.term: How is a branched substituent numbered and written?
cards.definition: Its carbon attached to the parent is C-1; its name goes in parentheses, e.g. 5-(2,2-dimethylpropyl)nonane
Prefix "cyclo" to the straight-chain alkane name

cards.text: Priority of functional groups: –COOH > –SO₃H > {{c1::–COOR}} > –COCl > {{c2::–CONH₂}} > –CN > {{c3::–CHO}} > >C=O > {{c4::–OH}} > –NH₂ > C=C > C≡C.

cards.definition: –R, halogens (F, Cl, Br, I), –NO₂, –OR
7-Hydroxyheptan-2-one (keto outranks hydroxyl), not 2-oxoheptan-7-ol
Ethane-1,2-diol (full "ethane" kept); buta-1,3-diene ("n" of -ane dropped)
3-Bromoprop-1-ene (double bond gets the lower number, not 1-bromoprop-2-ene)
5-Oxohexanoic acid: acid is principal, C-1 is the –COOH carbon
2-Chlorohexane: CH₃CHClCH₂CH₂CH₂CH₃. Pent-4-en-2-ol: CH₂=CHCH₂CH(OH)CH₃.

cards.term: In 3-nitrocyclohex-1-ene, why is C=C numbered before –NO₂?
cards.definition: C=C is a suffix group; –NO₂ is only a prefix

cards.term: Is the –CHO carbon counted in the parent chain?
cards.definition: Yes (5-hydroxyheptanal includes the CHO carbon as C-1)
Class, group, prefix, suffix and example for each family

cards.term: IUPAC names of toluene, anisole, aniline?
cards.definition: Methylbenzene, methoxybenzene, benzenamine (aminobenzene)
o = 1,2; m = 1,3; p = 1,4

cards.term: Can o/m/p be used for trisubstituted benzenes?
cards.definition: No: use lowest locants

cards.term: Name the benzene ring as a substituent.
cards.definition: Phenyl (C₆H₅–, Ph)
1-Chloro-2,4-dinitrobenzene (lowest locants, then alphabetical)
Two or more compounds with the same molecular formula but different properties
Chain: C₅H₁₂: pentane, isopentane, neopentane; Position: C₃H₈O: propan-1-ol, propan-2-ol; Functional group: C₃H₆O: propanal and propanone; Metamerism: C₄H₁₀O: methoxypropane and ethoxyethane

advancedHtml.backHtml:
Structural isomerism

Example?

ChainC₅H₁₂: pentane, isopentane, neopentane
PositionC₃H₈O: propan-1-ol, propan-2-ol
Functional groupC₃H₆O: propanal and propanone
MetamerismC₄H₁₀O: methoxypropane and ethoxyethane

cards.definition: Different alkyl chains on either side of the functional group

cards.term: Define stereoisomers and their two types.
cards.definition: Same constitution and bond sequence, different arrangement in space: geometrical and optical
Substrate: supplies carbon to the new bond. Reagent: the attacking species.
Step-by-step account of electron movement, energetics of bond breaking/forming and rates
Heterolytic: shared pair goes to one fragment → ions. Homolytic: one electron to each → free radicals.

cards.term: What is a carbocation and its old name?
cards.definition: Carbon with a sextet and positive charge; formerly carbonium ion
3° > 2° > 1° > CH₃⁺: (CH₃)₃C⁺ > (CH₃)₂CH⁺ > CH₃CH₂⁺ > CH₃⁺

cards.term: Shape and hybridisation of a carbocation?
cards.definition: Trigonal planar, sp²; empty p orbital perpendicular to the plane

cards.term: What is a carbanion, and its shape?
cards.definition: Carbon with a negative charge (lone pair); sp³, distorted tetrahedral

cards.term: Correction: NCERT calls the methyl carbanion a "distorted tetrahedron". Better description?
cards.definition: Trigonal pyramidal (like NH₃): the lone pair occupies the fourth sp³ position

cards.term: Stability order of alkyl free radicals?
cards.definition: 3° > 2° > 1° > methyl
Half-headed "fish-hook" curved arrow

cards.term: Other names for reactions via heterolysis and homolysis?
cards.definition: Heterolysis: ionic / polar. Homolysis: free radical / non-polar.
Nucleophile (Nu:, "nucleus-seeking"): brings an electron pair. Electrophile (E⁺): takes an electron pair.
HO⁻, NC⁻, R₃C⁻; neutral with lone pairs: H₂O, R₃N, R₂NH
Carbocations, carbonyl carbon (>C=O), carbon of alkyl halides (R₃C–X)

cards.term: Classify HS⁻, BF₃, C₂H₅O⁻, (CH₃)₃N, Cl⁺, CH₃C⁺=O, H₂N⁻, NO₂⁺. (Problem 8.12)
cards.definition: Nucleophiles: HS⁻, C₂H₅O⁻, (CH₃)₃N, H₂N⁻. Electrophiles: BF₃, Cl⁺, CH₃C⁺=O, NO₂⁺.

cards.term: Electrophilic centre in CH₃CH=O, CH₃CN, CH₃I? (Problem 8.13)
cards.definition: The carbon bonded to O, N or I (partial positive charge)

cards.term: Permanent vs temporary electron displacement effects?
cards.definition: Permanent: inductive, resonance (and hyperconjugation). Temporary: electromeric (only when a reagent attacks).
Polarisation of a σ bond caused by the polarisation of an adjacent σ bond

cards.term: How far does the inductive effect reach?
cards.definition: Falls off rapidly; negligible after three bonds
Halogens, –NO₂, –CN, –COOH, –COOR, –OAr
Alkyl groups: –CH₃, –CH₂CH₃

cards.term: More polar bond: H₃C–H or H₃C–Br; H₃C–NH₂ or H₃C–OH; H₃C–OH or H₃C–SH? (Problem 8.14)
cards.definition: C–Br; C–O; C–O

cards.term: Why isn’t benzene’s Kekulé structure adequate?
cards.definition: All C–C bonds are equal (139 pm), between C–C (154 pm) and C=C (134 pm)
Hypothetical structures that individually represent no real molecule; the real one is a hybrid
Both the same length, intermediate between N–O and N=O: a resonance hybrid
Energy difference between the actual hybrid and the lowest-energy canonical structure

cards.text: Resonance structures must have the same positions of {{c1::nuclei}} and the same number of {{c2::unpaired electrons}}.

cards.term: Which resonance structure is most stable?
cards.definition: More covalent bonds, all octets, less charge separation, negative charge on the more electronegative atom, more dispersal
Polarity from interaction of two π bonds, or a π bond with a lone pair on an adjacent atom; transmitted through the chain
Halogen, –OH, –OR, –OCOR, –NH₂, –NHR, –NR₂, –NHCOR (push electrons into the ring: aniline)
–COOH, –CHO, >C=O, –CN, –NO₂ (pull electrons: nitrobenzene)
Alternate single and double bonds: buta-1,3-diene, aniline, nitrobenzene; π electrons delocalised
Complete transfer of π electrons to one atom of a multiple bond on demand of an attacking reagent; temporary
+E: π electrons move to the atom the reagent attaches to. −E: to the atom it does not attach to.

cards.term: Inductive and electromeric effects in opposite directions: which wins?
cards.definition: Electromeric
Delocalisation of σ electrons of C–H of an alkyl group into an adjacent unsaturated system or empty p orbital; permanent

cards.term: Why is (CH₃)₃C⁺ more stable than CH₃CH₂⁺, and CH₃⁺ least? (Problem 8.19)
cards.definition: (CH₃)₃C⁺ has 9 C–H bonds for hyperconjugation; CH₃⁺’s C–H bonds lie perpendicular to its empty p orbital
No-bond resonance

cards.term: Mnemonic for which effects need a reagent? (intuition)
cards.definition: "E for Emergency": the Electromeric effect switches on only when a reagent arrives
Substitution, addition, elimination, rearrangement
Sharp melting or boiling point (now also chromatography and spectroscopy)
Separating sublimable compounds from non-sublimable impurities
Difference in solubility: compound sparingly soluble cold, well soluble hot
The filtrate left after crystallisation; contains impurities and a little compound

cards.term: How are coloured impurities removed during crystallisation?
cards.definition: Adsorption on activated charcoal
Volatile liquids from non-volatile impurities, or liquids with large b.p. difference (chloroform 334 K and aniline 457 K)
When b.p. difference is small; vapours pass through a fractionating column
Each successive condensation–vaporisation unit in a fractionating column
Separating fractions of crude oil

cards.term: Distillation under reduced pressure is used for?
cards.definition: Liquids with very high b.p. or that decompose below their b.p.; e.g. glycerol from spent-lye (soap industry)
Substances that are steam volatile and immiscible with water, e.g. aniline

cards.term: Why does a steam-distilled liquid boil below 373 K?
cards.definition: It boils when p₁ + p₂ = atmospheric pressure; p₁ < p, so below its own b.p.
Organic compound shaken with an immiscible organic solvent in which it is more soluble; separatory funnel

cards.term: What if the compound is poorly soluble in the organic solvent?
cards.definition: Continuous extraction: same solvent reused repeatedly
Greek "chroma" = colour: first used for plant pigments

cards.term: Two main types of chromatography by principle?
cards.definition: Adsorption and partition
Silica gel and alumina

cards.term: In column chromatography, where do strongly adsorbed substances stay?
cards.definition: Near the top of the column; the liquid that flows down is the eluant
\( R_f = \frac{distance \; moved \; by \; substance}{distance \; moved \; by \; solvent} \) (both from base line)
Silica gel or alumina, about 0.2 mm on glass (chromaplate)

cards.term: How are colourless spots on TLC detected?
cards.definition: UV light (fluorescence), iodine jar (brown spots), or spray reagent: ninhydrin for amino acids

cards.term: Paper chromatography: stationary and mobile phases?
cards.definition: Stationary: water trapped in the paper. Mobile: the solvent rising by capillary action.

cards.term: Is paper chromatography adsorption or partition?
cards.definition: Partition
Heat with CuO: CO₂ turns lime water milky; H₂O turns anhydrous CuSO₄ blue
Fuse with sodium to convert N, S, X into NaCN, Na₂S, NaX; boil with water = sodium fusion extract
Extract + FeSO₄, boil, acidify with conc. H₂SO₄ → Prussian blue Fe₄[Fe(CN)₆]₃·xH₂O
Acetic acid + lead acetate → black PbS; sodium nitroprusside → violet

cards.term: N and S both present: what forms and what colour?
cards.definition: NaSCN: with Fe³⁺ gives blood red [Fe(SCN)]²⁺; no Prussian blue

cards.term: How does excess sodium change the N+S result?
cards.definition: NaSCN + 2Na → NaCN + Na₂S: normal tests for N and S appear
Chlorine: White, soluble in NH₄OH; Bromine: Yellowish, sparingly soluble; Iodine: Yellow, insoluble in NH₄OH

advancedHtml.backHtml:
Halogen test (AgNO₃ after HNO₃)

Precipitate?

ChlorineWhite, soluble in NH₄OH
BromineYellowish, sparingly soluble
IodineYellow, insoluble in NH₄OH

cards.term: Why boil the extract with conc. HNO₃ before the halogen test?
cards.definition: To decompose NaCN and Na₂S, which would interfere with AgNO₃
Oxidise with Na₂O₂ to phosphate; HNO₃ + ammonium molybdate → yellow ammonium phosphomolybdate

cards.term: Estimation of C and H: absorbers?
cards.definition: Water in anhydrous CaCl₂; CO₂ in conc. KOH U-tubes

cards.term: Formulas for %C and %H (m₁ = CO₂, m₂ = H₂O, m = sample)?
cards.definition: \( \%C = \frac{12 \times m_1 \times 100}{44 \times m} \); \( \%H = \frac{2 \times m_2 \times 100}{18 \times m} \)

cards.term: 0.246 g gave 0.198 g CO₂ and 0.1014 g H₂O. %C, %H? (Problem 8.20)
cards.definition: C = 21.95%; H = 4.58%
Heat with CuO in CO₂ N oxides reduced on hot copper gauze collect N₂ over KOH (absorbs CO₂)
\( \%N = \frac{28 \times V_{STP} \times 100}{22400 \times m} \); pressure = atmospheric − aqueous tension

cards.term: 0.3 g gave 50 mL N₂ at 300 K, 715 mm (aq. tension 15 mm). %N? (Problem 8.21)
cards.definition: V(STP) = 41.9 mL → 17.46%
Heat with conc. H₂SO₄ → (NH₄)₂SO₄ add NaOH NH₃ absorbed in excess standard acid back-titrate
\( \%N = \frac{1.4 \times M \times 2(V - V_1/2)}{m} \)
Nitro, azo compounds and ring N (pyridine): their N does not form (NH₄)₂SO₄

cards.term: NH₃ from 0.5 g neutralised 10 mL of 1 M H₂SO₄. %N? (Problem 8.22)
cards.definition: = 20 mL 1 M NH₃ → 0.28 g N → 56.0%
Heat with fuming HNO₃ + AgNO₃ in a Carius tube; weigh AgX
\( \%X = \frac{atomic \; mass \; of \; X \times m_1 \times 100}{molar \; mass \; of \; AgX \times m} \)
Heat with Na₂O₂ or fuming HNO₃ in Carius tube → H₂SO₄ → weigh as BaSO₄: %S = 32 m₁ × 100 / (233 m)
42.10%
Oxidise to H₃PO₄; weigh as ammonium phosphomolybdate (%P = 31 m₁ × 100 / 1877 m) or Mg₂P₂O₇ (62 m₁ × 100 / 222 m)
By difference from 100%
Heat in N₂ pass over red-hot coke (→ CO) then warm I₂O₅: 5CO + I₂O₅ → I₂ + 5CO₂. %O = 32 m₁ × 100 / (88 m).

cards.term: Modern instrument for C, H, N?
cards.definition: CHN elemental analyser (needs only 1–3 mg)
